ideas.title: A bottom-bar quick-info widget, with one door anything can speak through
ideas.description:
Antonio, 2026-09-08, after seeing the refused-pick message land in the status bar: the bar should be a proper widget for short-lived information, styled, with a central API so a plugin or any component can put a line there.

WHAT EXISTS TODAY, AND WHY IT IS NOT THIS
`AppState.status_note: Option<String>` — added with P082(F003)/T475. A pick with nothing to offer writes one sentence there, `chrome_status` (heca/src/chrome/theme.rs) appends it to the status text, and the next keypress clears it (heca/src/app/input.rs, at the top of `handle_keyboard_input`). It works and it is deliberately plain, but it is:

- **a string on `AppState`, not a widget.** The whole bar is one `Label` built from `format!("{pane_count} panes | {focus_title} | {mode_str}{tail}")`. There is no styling to give a message, no icon, no severity, no room for two things at once, and no way to draw the message differently from the pane count beside it.
- **host-private.** `state.status_note = Some(..)` is reachable only from inside the app. A plugin has no way to say anything there, and neither does a component that is not holding `&mut AppState`. That is the ⭐⭐ RULE ZERO failure: there is no line a plugin author could write.
- **one message, last writer wins.** Two things with something to say silently overwrite each other.

The toast stack was tried first and rejected by Antonio for this case: a key that could not do its thing is not an event worth covering the work with an overlay. So the two are not substitutes — a notification is an *event*, this is a *reply to what you just did*, and they want different surfaces. Whatever is built here must not become a second notification system; see the note on ownership below.

WHAT TO BUILD (to be designed, not decided here)
- A **widget** in `heca-grid-ui` for the bar's transient region: domain-neutral, theme-driven, able to show a short line with a severity and optionally an icon, and to fold to nothing when there is nothing to say (`Visibility` already does the folding — see the rule on its entry in docs/widgets.md).
- **One door to speak through**, reachable from all three surfaces AGENTS requires: the app, a plugin, and RPC. The test is the one in RULE ZERO — write the line a plugin author would type. If it needs a registry, an id, or a host-private type, the API is missing.
- **A lifetime rule stated once.** Today's is "until the next keypress", which suits a reply to a key. A message from a background job wants something else — a duration, or until it is replaced. Whatever the answer, it belongs to the widget or the door, never to each caller: a rule every caller has to remember is the bug.
- **What happens when two things speak at once** — a queue, a priority, or a refusal. Today the second silently wins.

QUESTIONS TO SETTLE BEFORE BUILDING
- Is this the notification system's presentation for a `Toast`-unworthy severity, or a separate channel? Two systems that both put text on screen is exactly the "second path" AGENTS forbids — but a status reply and a notification genuinely differ in lifetime and in who dismisses them. Decide it explicitly rather than by which one gets built first.
- Does the bar keep its current fixed content (pane count | focus | mode) as segments, the way `[appearance.pane] title_segments` already configures the pane info bar? If so this is a segment kind, not a bolt-on, and the whole bar becomes configurable in the same breath.
- Who owns the bar's layout — is it a `ChromeRegion` with children, so a plugin could contribute a segment as well as a message?

WHERE THE CURRENT CODE IS
heca/src/chrome/theme.rs `chrome_status`; heca/src/app/render.rs `status_mode_parts`; heca/src/app_state.rs `status_note`; heca/src/app/input.rs (the clear); heca/src/handlers.rs `pick_refusal` (its first and only caller).

Once the door exists, `pick_refusal` should speak through it like anything else, and `status_note` should go.

ideas.title: A pane's actions and segments are a closed enum — nobody but the host can add one
ideas.description:
Raised by Antonio 2026-09-22 while deciding the region API (P082(F003)/T518). Leave the code as it is for now; this records what is wrong and the shape agreed for the fix.

THE DEFECT
`PaneAction` (Split, MoveLeft, MoveRight, Close, Zoom, Float) and `PaneSegment` (Location, AppName, PaneName, GitBranch, …) are closed Rust enums in `heca-config/src/appearance.rs`. `config.toml` picks from that list BY NAME, which reads like an open vocabulary and is not: a plugin cannot add an action or a segment at all, because there is no variant for it. Adding one means editing the host and recompiling it.

The pane header consumes them in `heca/src/chrome/pane_header.rs` — `content.actions` is `&[PaneAction]`, and `pane_action_spec` maps each variant to a glyph, a `WmAction`, a label and a focus rule.

WHY IT IS THE SAME DEFECT AS REGIONS
A fixed list the host owns, selected from by name, with no way for anyone else to contribute. That is exactly what T518 removes for a chrome region. Antonio, 2026-09-22: a plugin or another developer should add a pane action the way a provider is added to a sidebar —

    pane_actions::append(..).prepend(..).remove(..).retain(..)

and the same for segments. Internally that checks what `config.toml` asked for and builds the keys and ids itself, so no caller composes one.

THE ORDER, DECIDED
T518 (the region API) lands first and this reuses its shape — a handle fetched by name, `append`/`prepend`/`remove`/`retain`, placement and `.order` carried by the child, no index methods. Building this before T518 would write the same mechanism twice.

WHAT IT TOUCHES
- `heca-config/src/appearance.rs` — the two enums stop being the vocabulary. A configured name becomes a name, resolved against what was contributed.
- `heca/src/chrome/pane_header.rs` — `pane_action_spec`'s match is one contributor among others, not the whole list.
- The identity work in T474: an action's widget key is composed from the pane it belongs to plus the action's name, so a contributed action gets a correct key without its author knowing the rule.

⚠️ Not a licence to start. Propose the task and agree it when T518 is done.

ideas.title: Reusable configurable label segments and action buttons across components
ideas.description:
Captured at Antonio's explicit request as an IDEA ONLY. Implementation is intentionally deferred: this is not approval to implement, promote to a feature/phase/task, or expand P094.

Proposal
Provide reusable components for configured label segments and action buttons that can be composed anywhere: terminal headers, dock views, workspace rows, plugin content, and other surfaces. Register named information/label producers and actions once; each consuming component chooses its own ordered lists through config.toml rather than registration implicitly inserting UI into a universal pane header.

Illustrative configuration from the discussion (provisional names, not an agreed schema):
[settings.pane]
label_segments = ["git", "..."]

[settings.dockview]
label_segments = ["..."]
action_buttons = ["a", "b", "float"]

[settings.dockview.ws]
# Per-component or nested-surface choices.

The exact configuration root remains open: existing visual settings live under [appearance.*]. Do not migrate or add these keys merely because they are illustrated here.

Why
The current extension hooks pane_button, pane_chip and pane_line contribute to fixed built-in chrome surfaces. P094 makes pane content own its own optional header; browser/editor/plugin content may have no header at all. Reusable information and action components would separate the registered capability from its placement, so a consumer explicitly composes the UI where appropriate.

Existing pieces to reuse
- ActionCatalog/ActionRegistry remain the authority for actions, icons, labels, shortcuts, arguments and policy; avoid a competing action registry.
- Tag already renders segmented icon/text labels.
- ButtonGroup already renders grouped buttons.
- pane_items/listing.rs already centralizes configured ordering and default extension contributions.

Open design questions
- Public registration and composition API; names such as SegmentLabels and ButtonActions were suggestions, not decisions.
- How a consumer supplies plain context: which pane/workspace/directory a label reads and which target an action acts on, without host-private AppState or caller-maintained plumbing.
- Applicability and unavailable-data behavior across terminal, browser, editor and arbitrary plugin content; no implicit requirement that a Pane has a header.
- Per-component configuration scopes, reactivity, configuration reload, and compatibility with existing appearance.pane/title_segments/title_actions and appearance.sidebar/pane_lines.
- Native, declarative/plugin and RPC reachability through the established shared paths.

Relationship to existing work
I006 records the narrower original problem of closed pane-action/segment vocabularies; this idea concerns reuse and configurable placement across multiple components, beyond opening that vocabulary. I001 concerns a transient bottom-bar information channel and is separate.
P094(F011)/T450 owns terminal-header ownership; T452 owns generic pane content/creation; T454 proves a second content kind. This idea does not replace, duplicate, block or authorize changes to those tasks. A small rename of existing terminal-header/sidebar hooks was discussed separately, but is not implementation approval contained in this idea.

ideas.title: Table widget on demand for a concrete tabular UI consumer
ideas.description:
IDEA ONLY — preserved from P067(F003)/T253 at Antonio's explicit request on2026-10-29. The original task is closed as canceled; this is not scheduled work, an implementation approval or a prerequisite for P067/P094.

Consider a first-class Table only when an actual application/plugin consumer needs tabular behavior beyond existing composition. Original candidate capabilities: shared columns, a header, row selection and sorting. No concrete consumer was found in the reviewed Heca main/T398 sources. Grid/Row/Label already compose ordinary tables; CardGrid provides selectable cells and navigation, not a complete Table abstraction.

Before promotion, identify the consumer and the exact capability/reuse gap. Agree the public typed constructor/fluent composition and data/event contract; reuse Component, existing layouts/selection and the open host WidgetId/WidgetDefinition registry, never a new closed enum/dispatcher. Include native/described parity, showcase and central docs/widgets.md when a concrete task is approved.

History: T253 was explicitly on-demand and deferred by Antonio on2026-07-25 because its activation condition was not met. On2026-10-29 Antonio approved retaining it as an IDEA and closing the task. Preserve that original task history and link rather than treating the Table as implemented.

ideas.title: Scratchpad panes: a floating pane that stays hidden until toggled
ideas.description:
**Reviewed with Antonio 2026-11-17: KEEP.** Proposed shape (not yet agreed): build it as a case of one general "hide and show a pane without killing it" mechanism, not as a fourth separate pane state — a scratchpad is a hidden pane that reappears floating, toggled by one key, its process never stopping. The technical design is still to be discussed in detail with Antonio before any task.

Original text (from planning files that are now a historical archive):
- Old requirements file (LAY-03): "Scratchpad panes - hidden by default, toggled visible as floating". Also INP-05 (keyboard pane operations: kill, float, scratchpad, hide) and RPC-06 (pane.float, pane.embed, pane.scratchpad, pane.hide, pane.show).
- Old phase 2 context file (D-04): "Distinct states with dedicated keybinds. Every pane is in exactly one state: Embedded, Floating, Scratchpad (hidden until toggled), or Hidden. Each transition has a keybind. No automatic state changes."
- Old interaction-policy plan: "Scratchpad feature: may allow multiple floating panes" (open decision, moot until this exists).

State today (verified 2026-11-17): floating panes exist (action `float`); no scratchpad or hidden state in code. Found by the T561 gap report (M1). The niri column model has no scratchpad; i3/sway and tmux popups do. Related idea: hide/show a pane without killing it.

ideas.title: Hide and show a pane without killing it
ideas.description:
**Reviewed with Antonio 2026-11-17: KEEP, as its own idea (not merged with I012).** Antonio's picture: like minimizing a window on Windows and opening it again. The pane leaves the layout, its process keeps running, and when shown again it returns to its own column in its old place. Shares the underlying "hidden pane" mechanism with I012 (scratchpad, which instead reappears floating, toggled by one key) — build that mechanism once. Open design questions: where hidden panes are listed to restore them (sidebar mark, palette, both); exact restore position when the column changed meanwhile.

Original text (from planning files that are now a historical archive):
- Old requirements file (LAY-11): "Hide/show panes without killing them".
- Old phase 2 context file (D-04): pane states are Embedded, Floating, Scratchpad (hidden until toggled), or Hidden, each with a keybind.
- Old requirements file (RPC-06): pane.hide, pane.show.

State today (verified 2026-11-17): no pane-hide action in heca/src/actions; only region hide exists (hide_layer, show_left_sidebar and so on). Found by the T561 gap report (M2). Related idea: I012 scratchpad panes.

ideas.title: Layout templates: predefined TOML layouts, save the current layout, and layout.apply / layout.save_current over RPC
ideas.description:
**Reviewed with Antonio 2026-11-17: KEEP, adapted to today's heca** (niri-style columns and workspaces, not the old BSP split tree). Shape discussed: a named template describes workspaces, columns (with widths) and panes with the program each runs; applied by a key, the palette or RPC (e.g. `heca rpc layout_apply name=dev`); the current layout can be saved as a new template. Proposed (to confirm in design): reuse the format sessions are already saved in (heca.sessions.json carries name, folder, layout) rather than a second format; and allow a project to ship one (`.heca/`, under the existing project-trust rule). Design to be agreed with Antonio before any task.

Original text (from planning files that are now a historical archive; written for the old BSP tree):
- Old requirements file (LAY-04): "Predefined layout templates (TOML) applied to a tab".
- Old requirements file (LAY-05): "Save current tab layout as a named template".
- Old requirements file (RPC-07): "layout.apply, layout.save_current".
- Old phase 2 plan (Task 4.3): load templates from config_dir()/layouts/*.toml, for example
  name = "dev-session"
  root = { dir = "horizontal", ratio = 0.6, children = [ { title = "editor", app = "nvim" }, { dir = "vertical", ratio = 0.5, children = [ { title = "terminal", app = "terminal" }, { title = "files", app = "terminal" } ] } ] }
  with a serializable LayoutTemplate enum (Split, Pane { title, app }, Empty) and PaneTree::apply_template(template).
- Old features research file: lists predefined layouts as a differentiator.

State today (verified 2026-11-17): no template code. Related, existing: sessions are saved and restored with their layout (docs/sessions.md); per-project `.heca/config.toml` merges settings and keys only (docs/configuration.md). Found by the T561 gap report (M3).

ideas.title: Browser pane (CEF offscreen) and embedding arbitrary GUI windows, with the research table
ideas.description:
**Reviewed with Antonio 2026-11-17: KEEP, as a long-term idea.** Not to be started until terminal, layout and components are solid (as the old pitfall #7 says). When it comes, build it on the open pane-content composition of P094(F011) (a pane hosts any component); related: P106(F011)/T550 multi-document tabs lists browser pages as an example content, and heca-pro may open resources from chat.

The browser pane was deferred out of v1 on purpose (old project file: out of scope; decision "browser deferred to v2, CEF highest risk").

Original requirements (old requirements file, now a historical archive):
- BROW-01: Browser pane renders a real Chromium engine (CEF offscreen)
- BROW-02: Browser pane supports toggling DevTools as a sub-pane or attached window
- BROW-03: Browser pane forwards mouse and keyboard input to CEF
- ADV-01: Window embedding for arbitrary GUI apps (X11 reparenting, Windows SetParent, macOS NSView)

Research, verbatim from the old stack research file (Browser Plugin v2):
| Approach | Viability | Complexity | Notes |
| CEF offscreen (cef-rs / wef) | High | Very High | Renders Chromium to a shared texture. Cross-platform but ~100MB+ binaries. DevTools supported. |
| Platform WebView (wry) | Medium | High | Creates own window per webview. Hard to composite into our GPU surface without reparenting. |
| OS Window Reparenting | Medium | Very High | X11 XReparentWindow, Windows SetParent, macOS NSView addSubview. Platform-specific, fragile on Wayland. |
Recommendation: CEF offscreen for the browser plugin specifically. OS window embedding as a general plugin protocol for arbitrary GUI apps.

Pitfalls, verbatim from the old pitfalls research file:
- #7 CEF / Browser Plugin Blocking v1. Warning sign: spending months trying to embed Chromium before the core works. Prevention: Browser is explicitly v2. Do not touch CEF, webviews, or window reparenting until terminal + nvim + tiling are rock solid.
- #9 Wayland Window Embedding Complexity. Warning sign: "Window reparenting works on X11 and macOS but is impossible on Wayland." Prevention: Wayland does not allow arbitrary window reparenting. For Linux, prefer X11 for window-embedding plugins, or use xdg-shell surfaces with tight coordination. Document this limitation.

Also the old features research file lists "Browser pane (Chromium + DevTools): Very High, CEF offscreen rendering or window embedding" and "Out-of-process plugin protocol" as v2.

State today: no code, no planner task. Found by the T561 gap report (M6, M7, K4).

ideas.title: Advanced font features: variable font axes and stylistic sets
ideas.description:
**Reviewed with Antonio 2026-11-17: KEEP.** Proposed shape: (1) stylistic sets and other OpenType features first — a config list such as `font.features = ["ss01", "zero"]`, passed to cosmic-text, which already supports it (cosmic-text 0.19 `Attrs::font_features(FontFeatures)`, verified 2026-11-17); same path as the existing ligature policy. Cheap. (2) Variable font axes (e.g. `font.weight = 450`) second, after checking how far cosmic-text handles arbitrary axes. Would sit under F001/F002.

Original text (from the old requirements file, now a historical archive): ADV-03: "Advanced font features (variable axes, stylistic sets)".

State today: the ligature policy exists (P007(F002), terminal-02; heca-renderer/src/text/shape.rs and terminal/render.rs); variable axes and stylistic sets do not. Found by the T561 gap report (M8).

ideas.title: Multi-monitor: an action (with key binding) that sends the window to another monitor
ideas.description:
**Reviewed with Antonio 2026-11-17: KEEP, reduced to one thing:** a command that sends the current heca window to another monitor, as a registered action (so it reaches the palette, RPC and plugins like any other) with a default key binding, e.g. next/previous monitor and possibly "monitor N". Out of scope (decided): opening a new window on a chosen monitor.

How (verified 2026-11-17): heca never positions windows or reads monitors today; the OS places them. winit already offers available_monitors / current_monitor and set_outer_position (and fullscreen on a given monitor), which is all the action needs. Limit: on Linux Wayland the compositor decides window positions, so an app cannot move itself; only fullscreen on a chosen output is possible there — the action must report that instead of failing silently. Works on macOS, Windows and X11. Several windows per session already exist (P099(F012)/T545), so two monitors with two windows on one session works today by dragging.

Original text (from the old requirements file, now a historical archive): ADV-04: "Multi-monitor support (move windows between monitors)". Found by the T561 gap report (M9).

ideas.title: Layouts beyond niri: tabbed columns and vertically scrolling columns
ideas.description:
**Reviewed with Antonio 2026-11-17: KEEP two of the five, discard three.**
- KEEP 1 — tabbed column: only one pane of a column is visible, with a tab bar at its top to switch (niri has ColumnDisplay::Tabbed; old plan estimated it small). This is where the tab-bar slot on Pane (gridui-task-03, tabs.rs) would be consumed.
- KEEP 3 — vertically scrolling column: a column taller than the screen whose panes scroll up and down, instead of always sharing the height (fits heca's scroll-instead-of-shrink model).
- DISCARDED: horizontal panes inside a column (columns already do that), grid layout (columns + stacks already give it), column groups (overlaps workspaces).
It would be a heca-core layout feature (F006).

Original text (from planning files that are now a historical archive):
- Old niri analysis and plan, "What NIRI Does NOT Have": horizontal arrangement within a column; vertical scrolling within columns (tiles always fit height); grid layouts; mixed layout modes in one column. Marked as heca plans (Phase 2, Phase 3 optional, Future).
- Same file, "Phase 4: Advanced Layouts. Goal: extend beyond NIRI's model": 4.1 Horizontal column layout (panes side-by-side within a column, medium); 4.2 Tabbed/stacked columns (only the active pane visible with a tab bar, small); 4.3 Vertical column scrolling (scroll within tall columns, medium); 4.4 Grid layout (rows x cols grid within a column, medium); 4.5 Floating panes (shipped); 4.6 Column groups (named groups of columns, like niri workspaces but horizontal, large).
- Old backlog file (now a historical archive): "New feature surfaced: stacked/tabbed pane layout (niri/i3) - a heca-core LAYOUT feature that would consume tabs.rs; track under App/Chrome, not here."

Adjacent but different: P106(F011)/T550 (reusable multi-document tabs inside a pane), P050(F006)/T542 (pinned column). State today: no code, no planner task. Found by the T561 gap report (M10).

ideas.title: Shared sessions over SSH (tmux-style) and spring-based animations
ideas.description:
**Reviewed with Antonio 2026-11-17: KEEP both parts, reshaped.**

A — Shared sessions, tmux-style. Like tmux (one server + local socket; a remote person SSHes in and attaches; tmux knows nothing of networks or users, SSH does access and security), let a heca window on another computer attach to a session through SSH, which can forward a local Unix socket. heca already has the server, the socket, several windows per session and follow mode (P099/P104/T545). To check: behaviour under network latency, and a watch-only mode for guests. The VS Code Live Share form (accounts, share links, a cloud relay, guest permissions) is NOT for heca: proposed to heca-pro as its own idea (forwarded by Antonio).

B — Spring-based animations. Today every layout animation has a fixed duration and easing (heca-core/src/layout/animation.rs: AnimationConfig { duration_ms: 250, easing: ease_out_cubic }, verified 2026-11-17); niri uses springs. With a fixed duration, retargeting mid-animation (quick focus changes) restarts the motion and jerks; a spring keeps its velocity and stays smooth. Contained work: animations go through one AnimationConfig.

Original text (from the old features research file, now a historical archive), "v2 Features (Deferred)":
| Real-time collaboration / shared sessions | High | Multiple clients viewing the same session. |
| Advanced animations (physics-based resize) | Medium | GPU makes this possible, but not v1-critical. |
Found by the T561 gap report (M11).

ideas.title: [DISCARDED] Terminal scroll animation: sub-row pixel-smooth variant (B)
ideas.description:
**Discarded by Antonio 2026-11-17.** The whole-row animated scroll (variant A) stays as it is.

Original text (from the old backlog file, now a historical archive; entry terminal-task-01d, locked approach): "(A) integer-row step animated - visible_lines() keeps picking whole rows; the animated value rounds to the nearest row each frame. Zero renderer changes, Q6-safe (Full damage during the animation is fine). (B) sub-row pixel-smooth (renderer shifts content by a fractional row + clips partial rows) is DEFERRED to a follow-up - nicer but needs renderer work. Build A now; revisit B as polish." Found by the T561 gap report (M12).

ideas.title: Frame cost with many panes: whole-window layout runs every frame (follow-up of T421 and T562)
ideas.description:
Measured 2026-11-17 after T562 (PR #320): a release build with many panes and workspaces costs ~15 ms CPU per frame while interacting (HECA_FRAME_TIMES), against a 16.7 ms budget at 60 fps. Idle is ~0% and animations are smooth in release; a debug build stutters. The macOS sample shows most of each frame in paint_window -> paint_chrome_root -> LayoutEngine::compute/settle over the whole window tree, likely including content that is not on screen (other workspaces). Not proven which part.

History: P?/T421 measured the same unconditional layout (~3 ms in 2026-08). Attempt 1, a cache inside LayoutEngine::compute, was reverted: hosts mutate retained trees after layout (sync_pane_headers -> translate_tree moves header widgets every frame), so compute also resets bounds and cannot be skipped. A real fix needs those post-layout moves to become idempotent or part of layout (as ScrollRegion's on_layout already does), then a dirty check in the library.

Same class, small: a focused text field inside a hidden panel still wakes the loop twice a second for its caret blink (bounded, low rate). Fix it like the T562 flash fix: a wake booked by a widget nobody paints lapses.

Tools: HECA_FRAME_REASONS (why each frame was asked for) and HECA_FRAME_TIMES (CPU per frame). Related: T148 (stop unconditional per-frame clear).

ideas.title: Which-key popup: after the prefix (or a chord), show the keys you can press next
ideas.description:
From phase P073(F010) "WhichKey Like Modal", turned into an idea by Antonio on 2026-11-17 (the phase was a draft with no tasks; its only text was the summary "Implement a neovim emacs wich-key feature like.").

Like Neovim's which-key and Emacs' which-key: after pressing the prefix (or the first key of a chord/mode), a small popup lists the keys available next and what each does, so nobody has to memorise the table.

State today (checked 2026-11-17): `heca --keys-show` prints every binding from the command line (docs/keyboard-commands.md § "Finding a key"), and the status bar shows the current mode, but nothing lists the next keys in the window after the prefix. To design: when it appears (immediately or after a short delay), where (overlay near the status bar), grouping by action category, and that the list comes from the one keymap (bindings, modes, plugin-contributed actions), never a second hand-written table.

ideas.title: Package managers: Homebrew, maybe AUR, maybe winget or Chocolatey
ideas.description: From Antonio, 2026-11-18, while planning the first release workflow (phase "Build and release" in F010). After the GitHub Release with zips and installers exists: publish heca through package managers — Homebrew (macOS, and Linux), maybe AUR (Arch Linux), maybe winget or Chocolatey (Windows). Each would consume the release's artifacts on every tag. Not approved work; to discuss when the release workflow is in use. Related: signing/notarization (also deferred) affects Homebrew casks and winget.
